title: Pick the timing/length: walk 6/8/10/12, run 6/8/10, idle 8/12/16 (snappy holds vs even), jump anticipation/hang short vs long
question: Owner: 'test different timings and lengths for the animation depending on the action; we want more expression, bouncy, liveliness'. Which frame count and timing feel per action?
method: 24 motion variants (motion/variants/, scripts/mvariants.py): the same round-3 motion sampled phase-correctly at different frame counts; 'snappy' puts samples on key poses so display times become holds (walk holds the passing pose), 'even' is uniform. Jump: crouch hold x0.5/x2.5 and apex hang x0.6/x1.8 (time-warped keys, springs in real time). Each rendered through R's renderer + P's pixel chain (SE) and as smooth previews (SE, E). Labelled grid GIFs on 20 ms ticks (every frame >= 20 ms, loop = cycle).
result: pxeval boil (gate .02): walk 8/10/12 .005-.018 pass, walk 6 .033; idle all pass (.009-.016); run .05 (10 fr) to .12 (6 fr); jump ~.075. More frames = less boil. shade_swap fails everywhere (P's chain).
verdict: Owner to pick one cell per action (letters in each grid). M's suggestion: walk 10 snappy or 8 snappy, run 8 snappy (10 for smoothness), idle 12 holds, jump long anticipation + long hang.
